Package frc.robot.subsystems.drivetrain.module

Class ModuleIO

java.lang.Object
frc.robot.subsystems.drivetrain.module.ModuleIO
Direct Known Subclasses:
ModuleReplay, ModuleSpark
public abstract class ModuleIO extends Object
Abstract base class defining the interface for swerve drive module implementations.

Each swerve module independently controls:

  • Drive velocity (forward/backward wheel speed)
  • Turn position (wheel orientation/direction)

This class defines the contract that all swerve module implementations must follow. Concrete implementations (e.g., ModuleSpark) handle specific hardware configurations (motor types, encoders, controllers).

The module tracks state via ModuleIO.ModuleData which includes:

  • connection status
  • position
  • velocity
  • voltage
  • current

The Drivetrain subsystem uses module implementations via dependency injection to support different hardware configurations or simulation.

  • Method Details

    • update

      public abstract void update()
      Reads sensor data from motors and encoders, updating ModuleIO.ModuleData. This method should be called periodically (typically in subsystem periodic) to refresh all sensor readings in the module data. Drive position and turn position must be continuously integrated from encoder values.

    • setDesiredState

      public void setDesiredState(edu.wpi.first.math.kinematics.SwerveModuleState desired)
      Sends desired module state commands to the hardware.

      This method takes a desired swerve module state (velocity and angle) and sends the appropriate commands to the drive and turn motors. The state includes:

      • speedMetersPerSecond: Target drive motor velocity
      • angle: Target turn motor direction/orientation

      The Drivetrain subsystem calls this method with optimized and cosine-scaled states to minimize wheel slip and ensure smooth motion. This method should:

      1. Apply any hardware-specific control loop gains
      2. Clamp commands to safe ranges
      3. Send setpoints to motor controllers
      Parameters:
      desired - The target state including velocity and wheel angle

    • setStateSetpoint

      public abstract void setStateSetpoint(double driveVelocity, double turnPosition)
      Sends direct velocity and position setpoints to motor controllers. This is the low-level command method called by setDesiredState(SwerveModuleState). Implementations should send these values to the appropriate motor controllers (velocity control for drive, position control for turn).
      Parameters:
      driveVelocity - Target drive motor velocity in meters per second
      turnPosition - Target turn motor position in radians

    • getPosition

      public final edu.wpi.first.math.kinematics.SwerveModulePosition getPosition()
      Gets the current position of this module (drive distance and turn angle).

      This position is used by the Drivetrain's SwerveDrivePoseEstimator for tracking robot pose based on wheel movement (odometry). The position includes:

      • Drive distance: Total distance wheel has traveled (meters)
      • Angle: Current orientation of the wheel (radians)
      Returns:
      Current swerve module position from sensor data
